stock.reason: No candidate qualified today. The test that removed the most was book-full: all 21 position slots are already open — 3,232 of 3,232 screened.
stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.

stories.title: Converting Documents to Markdown With MarkItDown
stories.excerpt: Learn how to use MarkItDown to convert Excel files, PDFs, and images into clean Markdown that's ready for LLMs and AI workflows.
stories.lead:
The MarkItDown library lets you quickly turn PDFs, Office files, images, HTML, and URLs into LLM-ready Markdown. In this video course, you’ll install MarkItDown, use it in Python code to convert and batch-process documents, connect it to AI clients through its MCP server, and see where it falls short compared to tools like Pandoc.

By the end of this course, you’ll understand that:

With this foundation, you’ll be able to judge when MarkItDown is the fastest route from raw files to useful LLM context and when your project calls for a heavier-duty conversion workflow.

stories.title: Hakeem Jeffries is poised to become the first Black speaker of the House
stories.excerpt: As speaker, the New York Democrat would be second in the presidential line of succession, after the vice president. He has vowed to focus on affordability and holding the administration accountable.
stories.lead:
Midterms coverage: Live results | What to know | Stories around the countryStay connected: NPR Politics Podcast | NPR Politics newsletter | NPR app

After helping to deliver a decisive victory for House Democrats in the midterm elections, Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., appears all but certain to become the first Black lawmaker to be elected speaker of the House.

Jeffries was elected House minority leader in 2022 and is the first Black politician to lead either party in the House or Senate. As speaker, Jeffries would be second in the presidential line of succession, after the vice president.

stories.lead:
Just under a third of households have a mortgage, according to the government's English Housing Survey, external.

About 500,000 homeowners have a mortgage that "tracks" the Bank of England's rate.

Any rise in the Bank rate means an increase in the monthly repayments on their outstanding loan. For a typical loan, the cost would go up by about £31 a month if the Bank raises the base rate by 0.25 percentage points, but it depends on the size of people's loans.

stories.title: Uproar over missing 'pop' as Rice Krispies changes its recipe
stories.excerpt: The new recipes mean cereal packaging will now include a 'contains wheat gluten' warning.
stories.lead:
Rice Krispies and Coco Pops, long-standing staples of the family breakfast table, will no longer be made of whole rice grains in the UK, after Kellogg's said it was changing its recipe.

Instead the tiny toasted puffs will be made using corn flour and rice flour, and will also now contain wheat gluten as an ingredient.

A Kellogg's spokesperson said the reformulation was due to "changing weather conditions" that have disrupted supplies of some grains and cereals.
